text: dsh-auto-model-router 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的模型路由插件。它挂接 agent 请求与会话生命周期，并提供 Auto 虚拟模型入口，把每次用户输入分配到用户配置的 L0–L3 模型层级。功能包括按输入长度启发式选择、按关键词规则评分、可选的 LLM 任务分类、成本模式和会话 token 预算控制，以及请求失败后的模型回退链。它适合希望按任务复杂度在模型间切换、平衡响应质量与成本的 DSH 用户。无需单独填写插件 API key；路由使用 DSH 的 LLM 服务。

dsh-auto-model-router routes DSH web requests among configured L0–L3 models through a virtual Auto choice. It supports input-width heuristics, keyword rules, optional LLM classification, cost modes, token budgets, and fallback routes. It uses DSH’s LLM service and needs no separate plugin API key.
我想让 DSH 根据任务难度自动选不同档位的模型。
有没有办法按输入长短切换模型？
想用关键词规则决定请求走哪个模型。
希望复杂任务用强模型，简单问题用便宜模型。
能不能给每个会话设 token 预算并在超额后降级？
模型请求失败时，想自动尝试备用模型。
Route each DSH request to a model based on the task complexity.
I want keyword rules to choose which model handles a request.
dsh-auto-model-router 的功能「自动模型入口」：插件注册 Auto 虚拟 provider；在模型选择器选 Auto 后，agent 请求由路由器分配到配置的 L0–L3 模型。
dsh-auto-model-router 的功能「按输入选择层级」：对每个新用户输入作一次路由决策，可结合输入宽度启发式、固定层级或全自动规则与分类器模式。
dsh-auto-model-router 的功能「成本控制与预算」：按 cost-first、quality-first 或 balanced 模式确定默认层级和歧义时的漂移方向；会话 token 预算耗尽时可固定到低成本层级。
dsh-auto-model-router 的功能「请求失败回退」：agent 请求失败时按配置的 fallback chain 尝试下一个模型路由。
dsh-auto-model-router 的功能「状态与配置提示」：会话开始时发送当前路由状态，并可提供浏览器设置页读取的路由状态接口。

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · dsh-auto-model-router：A hybrid auto model-router plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). Routes each agent request through **four capability levels (L0–L3)** with three user-facing routing modes: a zero-latency **heuristic lock** (text-width thresholds), a **fixed-level** mode, and **fully-auto** mode (keyword scoring + optional LLM classifier). Failure fallback chains and budget control round it out.

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · dsh-auto-model-router：> Design inspired by [open-world-project/model-router](https://github.com/open-world-project/model-router) (Hermes Agent) and [opencode-model-router](https://github.com/marco-jardim/opencode-model-router) (fast/medium/heavy tiers): tiered routing plus a cost mode that decides the drift direction on ambiguity.

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Acknowledgements：- [open-world-project/model-router](https://github.com/open-world-project/model-router) — Hermes Agent's auto model-router with keyword scoring and cost-aware tier selection

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · How it works：One decision is made **per user input** (not per agent step). Steps within the
same input reuse the decision — the LLM classifier is never called per step.

```
user input (new)
  │
  ▼
┌─ current mode?

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · The four levels：| Level | Typical tasks | Model guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `L0` | everyday chat, quick answers | cheapest/fastest |
| `L1` | small edits, simple tests | regular |
| `L2` | writing code, review, refactoring | strong |
| `L3` | complex bug fixes, multi-step tasks, reports | most powerful |

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · The four levels：Each level is a user-assigned provider/model route with a **required**
`reasoningEffort` (defaults to `off` when omitted): `off` = no thinking mode,
`high`/`max` = thinking intensity. Levels may be left unconfigured; the router
then falls to the nearest configured level (direction depends on the cost
mode).

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Auto mode in the model selector：The plugin registers a virtual `auto` provider, so the model selector shows an
**Auto Router** group with a single **Auto** model:

```
Auto Router
  └─ Auto
deepseek-official
  ├─ deepseek-v4-flash

- Pick **Auto** → this plugin routes the session through the L0–L3 levels.
- Pick any **real model** → the plugin passes the request through untouched;
  your explicit choice wins and the router stays out of the way.

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Settings section (browser)：The browser half registers an **Auto Router** page in DSH's settings panel
(gear icon → sidebar). It renders the current routing policy — the same
`<dsh-auto-model-router-status>` report the host injects on session start —
with a hint telling you to change the configuration through AI conversation:
just tell the agent in chat (e.g. *"change L2 to deepseek-v4-flash with max
reasoning"* or *"switch cost mode to cost-first"*), and the AI edits
`cordis.patch.yml` for you; restart DSH to apply.

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Settings section (browser)：Selecting **Auto** in the model picker applies immediately — there is no
confirmation dialog.

No client build step is needed: `client.js` is a self-contained ModuleLoader
bundle maintained in this repository (`pnpm run build:client` regenerates it
from `client/`).

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-auto-model-router
```

Or via the published npm package:

```bash
npm install @adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router
dsh plugin --profile web add @adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router
```

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Configuration：Add to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-auto-model-router
      name: '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group'
      group: true

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · costControl modes：| mode | default level (no rule hit) | ambiguity drift |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cost-first` | lowest configured level | **down** (cheaper) |
| `quality-first` | highest configured level | **up** (stronger) |
| `balanced` | `costControl.defaultLevel` | stay put |

A rule hit always wins over the cost mode: a level the user explicitly matched
is never downgraded by the cost layer.

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Budget downgrade is visible：- e.g. `tokenBudgetPerSession: 300000`: downgrade once the session uses 300k tokens.
- The downgrade behavior is controlled by `downgradeBehavior` (default `notify`):
  - `notify`: inject a user-visible message explaining the budget is exhausted,
    which model the remaining requests use, and how to raise the cap.
  - `ask`: pop a dialog asking "switch to the cheaper model or keep the current
    one?"; choosing "keep" waives the budget for the rest of the session.
  - `silent`: switch silently (not recommended — the user wonders why answers
    got worse).

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · On-load consultation (no client UI)：On the **first session** after installing or hot-reloading the plugin, DSH:

1. Injects a status report message (level→model mapping, cost mode, budget,
   fallback chain). The language follows `settings.yaml`'s
   `locale.preference` (`zh`/`en`, default `en`).
2. Pops a dialog with three questions (asked once per plugin load):

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · On-load consultation (no client UI)：| Question | Options |
| --- | --- |
| Q1 Tier-1 rules | Keep current rules / **View current rules** (injects the rule list) |
| Q2 Tier-2 cost mode | Keep current / cost-first / balanced / quality-first (applies immediately) |
| Q3 Other config | Skip / **Check a setting** (type budget, fallbackChain, classifier, …; injects its current value) |

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Rule syntax：- Plain text: `match: 'refactor'` — case-insensitive substring.
- Regex literal: `match: '/\\bdebug\\b/'` — slashes delimit the pattern, optional flags after the last slash (`/.../i`).
- Rules are evaluated **in order**; the first match wins.
- `match` can target user message text, tool-call results text, or the session `cwd` (matched as `cwd:<path>`).

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · What the plugin hooks：| DSH event | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `agent/session-start` | reset per-session routing state |
| `agent/pre-step` | token accounting for budget tracking |
| `system-prompt/assemble` | keep `{{model}}` prompt variables consistent |
| `agent/request` | **the routing decision** — replace provider/model |
| `agent/request-error` | fallback chain → `{ kind: 'retry' }` |
| `session/event` | track spend from assistant messages |

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Testing：```bash
npm test        # node --test *.test.mjs
```

No external services are required — all layers are unit-tested against fixtures.

@adverts13/dsh-auto-model-router README · Known Issues：- **Fully-auto mode latency**: When the LLM classifier is enabled, the first
  step of each new user input incurs an additional LLM call (classification).
  While subsequent steps within the same input are cached and fast, the overall
  round-trip for multi-step tasks is noticeably slower than directly selecting
  a model. Contributions to optimize this are welcome — the classifier could
  potentially be cached across sessions, or a lighter heuristic could be used
  as a first pass before falling back to the LLM.
